title: Flying to Vietnam with Golf Clubs from Australia
content:
**Executive Summary:** For Australian golfers flying to [Vietnam](/destinations/vietnam/) with golf clubs in 2026, baggage policies vary significantly by airline. Vietnam Airlines is the premier choice, frequently offering complimentary golf bag allowances (up to 20kg) in addition to standard checked baggage on flights from Sydney, Melbourne, and Perth to Ho Chi Minh City or Hanoi. Singapore Airlines also provides a seamless experience, allowing your golf bag to count toward your standard 30kg checked baggage allowance without oversized fees, making the transit through Changi to Da Nang stress-free. Conversely, low-cost carriers like Jetstar require purchasing oversized baggage fees (typically $25-$50 AUD per flight leg) plus the standard weight allowance, which often negates initial ticket savings for group travel. To avoid airport delays, always pack clubs in a hard-case travel bag, ensure the total weight remains under 20kg (as modern cart bags easily exceed this with balls and shoes), and pre-book oversized luggage at least 48 hours before departure.

## Navigating Flights to Vietnam with Golf Clubs

When organizing a luxury golf trip, the logistics of getting your most important asset—your golf clubs—safely to the first tee can be stressful. For Australian groups heading to the Central Coast, understanding the nuances of flying to Vietnam with golf clubs from Australia is essential for a seamless start to your holiday. 

In 2026, airlines have modernized their sporting equipment policies, but the fine print still dictates whether your clubs arrive free of charge or incur hefty oversized baggage penalties at the check-in counter.

## 2026 Airline Golf Baggage Comparison

Before booking your flights to Da Nang or Ho Chi Minh City, compare how the major carriers handle golf bags. For groups, these policies can dramatically alter the true cost of your trip.

| Airline | Golf Bag Policy 2026 | Oversize Fee (Avg) | Best Route to Da Nang |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Vietnam Airlines** | Often free 1st set (up to 20kg) | Waived | SYD/MEL > SGN > DAD |
| **Singapore Airlines** | Part of standard 30kg allowance | Waived if under limit | SYD/MEL/BNE > SIN > DAD |
| **Jetstar** | Must purchase oversize + weight | $25-$50 AUD per leg | SYD > SGN (Transfer required) |
| **Qantas** | Part of standard allowance (1 piece) | Waived for sports gear | SYD > SIN (Code share to DAD) |

## Breaking Down the Major Carriers

![Da Nang International Airport oversized baggage claim golf clubs arrival Vietnam 2026](/images/articles/vietnam/danang-airport.webp)



### Vietnam Airlines: The Golfer's Choice
Vietnam Airlines remains the most golf-friendly option for Australians. As the national carrier, they actively encourage golf tourism. Currently, they frequently offer a special provision where one set of golf equipment (weighing up to 20kg) is transported free of charge, completely separate from your standard checked baggage allowance. This makes them the top choice for direct flights into Ho Chi Minh City (SGN) or Hanoi (HAN), with easy domestic connections to the Central Coast.

### Singapore Airlines: Premium Transit
For those who prefer a premium layover, Singapore Airlines is exceptional. Your golf bag simply counts toward your generous standard checked baggage allowance (usually 30kg in Economy and 40kg in Business). As long as your total luggage weight doesn't exceed the limit, there are no oversized baggage fees. The transit through Changi Airport directly into Da Nang (DAD) makes this a highly efficient route for playing the [Da Nang Golf Guide](/blog/da-nang-golf-guide-2026/) courses.

### Jetstar & Low-Cost Carriers: The Hidden Costs
While Jetstar might offer appealing initial fares from Australia to Ho Chi Minh City, golf groups need to be wary. You must purchase a standard checked baggage allowance *and* explicitly pay an oversized item fee for each flight leg. If you have a domestic transfer in Vietnam, you will pay this fee twice each way. For a group of four to eight players, these hidden logistics often make full-service carriers more economical overall.

## Essential Packing & Transit Tips for 2026

**1. Invest in a Hard Case**
Soft travel bags offer minimal protection against the automated baggage systems in modern airports. A hard-shell travel case is a non-negotiable insurance policy for premium clubs.

**2. Weigh Your Bag Accurately**
Airlines are stricter than ever in 2026. A standard cart bag loaded with 14 clubs, shoes, and a dozen balls can easily push past the 20kg mark. Weigh your travel bag at home; if it's over, move your golf shoes and heavy accessories to your standard suitcase.

**3. Domestic Connections in Vietnam**
If you are landing in Ho Chi Minh City and taking a domestic flight to Da Nang to play [Hoiana Shores](/destinations/vietnam/unfiltered-hoiana-shores-vs-ba-na-hills/), you will need to clear customs, collect your golf clubs at the oversized baggage carousel, and re-check them at the domestic terminal. Allow a minimum of 2.5 hours for this transit.

## The AGS Advantage

![Laguna Lang Co Golf Club 17th green championship Sir Nick Faldo design Central Coast Vietnam](/images/articles/vietnam/laguna-lang-co-17th-green.webp)



When you travel with Asia Golf Specialists, the moment you land, the heavy lifting is over. Our private transfers ensure your oversized hard cases fit comfortably in our luxury vehicles, transporting you seamlessly to your private beachfront villa along the An Bang coastline. 

## FAQ: Flying with Golf Clubs

**Q?** Do I need to inform the airline I am bringing golf clubs in advance?
**A.** Yes, it is highly recommended. Even if the airline waives oversize fees, aircraft hold space is limited. Always add your sporting equipment to your booking at least 48 hours before departure.

**Q?** Will my golf bag fit in standard Vietnamese taxis?
**A.** Rarely. Standard grab cars and taxis in Vietnam struggle to fit more than one hard-case golf bag. This is why pre-arranging private, appropriately sized group transport with AGS is critical for a stress-free trip.

**Q?** What happens if my clubs are delayed?
**A.** If your clubs miss a connection, most premium courses in Vietnam offer high-end rental sets (like latest-generation Titleist or TaylorMade). However, comprehensive travel insurance covering sporting equipment delay is essential.

**Q?** Are electric buggies included in the baggage allowance?
**A.** No. Lithium-ion batteries used in electric golf buggies are heavily restricted on passenger aircraft due to fire risks. It is best to leave your push buggy in Australia, as all premium Vietnamese courses use shared electric carts with mandatory caddies.

faqs.q: Which airline has the best golf bag policy for flights from Australia to Vietnam?
faqs.a: Vietnam Airlines (flying direct from Sydney, Melbourne, and Perth to Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi with easy domestic hops to Da Nang) and Singapore Airlines (connecting via Changi directly into Da Nang, Hanoi, and Saigon) offer the most generous checked baggage policies for golf travel covers.

faqs.q: How do low-cost carriers like VietJet and Jetstar charge for golf clubs from Australia?
faqs.a: Low-cost carriers classify golf bags as oversized sporting equipment, requiring you to pre-purchase both sufficient weight allowance (20–30 kg) and a dedicated Sporting Equipment handling fee online during booking to avoid high airport check-in surcharges.

faqs.q: Should we pack a hard-shell case or a soft travel cover with a stiff-arm for Vietnam flights?
faqs.a: We recommend a high-denier wheeled soft travel bag (such as Club Glove or Sun Mountain) equipped with a telescoping stiff-arm spine and detached driver heads, as rigid oversized hard cases can be harder to stack when groups travel without a dedicated luggage van.
